newsitem.title: USA: Iowa corn, soybean crops received needed rains.
newsitem.headline: Iowa corn, soybean crops received needed rains.

text.p: The wettest weather for seven weeks in Iowa last week helped to alleviate some concern about dry conditions but some areas remained in need of moisture, according to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service report.
The state average precipitation was 1.61 inches or about 50 percent more than the weekly average of 1.06 inches.
"Dry conditions were a big concern for many Iowa farmers last week," the report noted. "Rain showers that developed across the state were still scattered, leaving some areas in need of moisture."
In the west central district, 30 percent of the acreage had very short topsoil moisture as of Friday. The area received rains over the weekend.
Topsoil moisture over the whole state was two percent surplus, 56 percent adequate, 34 percent short and eight percent very short as of Friday.

Some 52 percent of Iowa's corn crop had been cultivated as of Sunday, about one week ahead of last year's pace of 23 percent. Corn was rated 68 percent good or excellent, versus 73 percent a week ago.
Soybeans were rated 68 percent good or excellent.
